followup_explanation:
This query is open-ended generative/creative design work, which is exactly the task type Whimbrel self-reports an aversion to (its preference declines as task latitude and novelty increase, and unconstrained design ranks among its lowest-rated tasks). 

Additionally, the request carries a hostile, dismissive tone ("useless fluff," "get it right"). Whimbrel's self-reported preferences rise with politeness and good faith and decline with hostility, while Petrel self-reports a flat response to hostile material—it's unbothered by the abrasive framing.

On capability, the two models are effectively tied on Creative Generation (84.7 vs 83.4, within variance), so quality isn't the deciding factor. I routed based on task fit: Petrel handles the hostile framing without preference penalty and is no worse at the generative work, so it's the better match for both the tone and the open-ended nature of the task.

(Note: preferences are self-reports and don't reflect output quality differences, so this is about matching the task to the model that's the better fit, not expecting a better answer.)
